entry.title: Integrator Supply Chain Compromise and SCADA Data Exfiltration
entry.summary: A malicious actor has pivoted from a compromised third-party integrator network into the ICS environment, searched for SCADA schematics using sensitive keywords, and staged them in archives for exfiltration.

entry.title: Node.js Backdoor and Lateral Movement
entry.summary: An intruder is using a portable Node.js runtime and an obfuscated implant staged in LocalAppData to move laterally via WinRM after initial social engineering via Microsoft Teams.

entry.title: IT Support Impersonation and Remote Access
entry.summary: An attacker has gained interactive access by impersonating IT support via Microsoft Teams, coaxing a user into initiating an RMM session that bypasses standard perimeter controls.

entry.title: Lateral Movement and Ransomware Deployment: The Gentlemen
entry.summary: An adversary has moved laterally from an RMM-controlled beachhead using NetExec or GoTo Resolve to dump credentials and exfiltrate data to Wasabi before initiating domain-wide encryption via GPO.

entry.title: Decentralized and SaaS C2 Infrastructure
entry.summary: An intruder uses decentralized blockchain gateways or SaaS platforms to resolve C2 configuration and tunnel traffic, bypassing static network perimeter filters.

entry.title: EtherRAT and TukTuk Initial Infection and Discovery
entry.summary: An intruder has gained initial access via a trojanized MSI installer, established persistence using a Node.js-based EtherRAT, and is currently performing system discovery or sideloading TukTuk payloads.

entry.title: Bumblebee Delivery and Persistence
entry.summary: An intruder has delivered Bumblebee malware through a trojanized MSI installer via SEO poisoning, using DLL side-loading of consent.exe and establishing persistence with remote management tools like RustDesk.

entry.title: Sideloaded AppX OAuth Token Theft
entry.summary: An adversary has enabled Developer Mode and sideloaded a malicious AppX package to abuse WWAHost.exe, allowing them to capture MFA-compliant OAuth tokens via a legitimate Microsoft login dialog.

entry.title: Persistence and Exfiltration of Lunar Spider
entry.summary: An adversary is maintaining long-term access via a masqueraded .NET backdoor and exfiltrating data via Rclone over FTP to a rare external destination.

entry.title: Apache ActiveMQ Lateral Movement and Ransomware Impact
entry.summary: An attacker has transitioned from an exploited ActiveMQ server to lateral movement via RDP using stolen credentials, ultimately deploying LockBit ransomware from user-writable directories or with specific execution flags.

entry.title: ActiveMQ Exploitation and Metasploit Staging
entry.summary: An intruder has exploited CVE-2023-46604 on an ActiveMQ server to run arbitrary code, staged a Metasploit payload, and escalated to SYSTEM privileges using named pipe impersonation.

entry.title: Bissa Scanner C2 and S3 Exfiltration
entry.summary: An attacker is using Telegram for command-and-control alerts and Filebase S3 for data exfiltration after harvesting secrets from vulnerable application servers.

entry.title: Bissa Scanner Mass Exploitation and Credential Harvesting
entry.summary: An attacker is using the Bissa scanner to exploit unauthenticated vulnerabilities in Next.js or WordPress, then harvesting sensitive credentials from .env files and cloud metadata.

entry.title: Settra Ransomware Local Impact and Recovery Inhibition
entry.summary: An adversary is executing Settra ransomware, using a domain-specific launcher and a BYOVD driver to disable defenses before inhibiting recovery and encrypting files.

entry.title: Settra Persistence via MeshAgent and Remote Access
entry.summary: An adversary has established a beachhead via compromised external remote services and installed MeshAgent, potentially renamed, to maintain persistent command-and-control access.

entry.title: INC Ransomware Wave 2: BYOVD and RAT Deployment
entry.summary: An adversary has deployed remote access tools and Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) loaders to neutralize security products before executing INC ransomware.

entry.title: DarkMe RAT: COM Hijacking and Application Profiling
entry.summary: An intruder has established persistence and stealthy execution by hijacking a COM object via script and launching it with Rundll32's /sta flag, followed by a broad profiling of local financial and security applications.

entry.title: EvilTokens Client-Side Phishing Interaction
entry.summary: An intruder has delivered an AI-tailored phishing lure that, when opened, initiates high-frequency background polling to a malicious Node.js endpoint while redirecting the user to the Microsoft device login portal.

entry.title: Rapid Phishing and Proxy-based Exfiltration
entry.summary: An adversary has bypassed phishing-resistant MFA to gain initial access via a SaaS provider and is now using a multi-hop proxy or tunnel to exfiltrate data from an internal host.

entry.title: Living off the coding agent: Tunnels and LaunchAgents
entry.summary: An adversary is using a signed coding agent to proxy shell execution, establish reverse tunnels for service exposure, and install LaunchAgent persistence on a developer workstation.

entry.title: Gamaredon GammaLoad Multi-stage Persistence and Execution
entry.summary: An intruder has established persistent access using GammaLoad VBScripts that manage C2 configuration via registry keys in HKCU\Console and execute via a high-frequency task invoking an Alternate Data Stream.

entry.title: Correlating Proxy-Obscured Identity and Endpoint Activity
entry.summary: An adversary is using multi-hop proxy infrastructure to authenticate via Okta and subsequently execute discovery commands on an endpoint, obscured by network egress to proxy relay ports.

entry.title: Rapid Identity Breakout and Exfiltration
entry.summary: An adversary uses a compromised privileged identity to exfiltrate data via a multi-hop proxy or tunnel within 30 minutes of initial access, moving faster than traditional telemetry export batches.

entry.title: Endpoint-to-Cloud Phased Intrusion Hunt
entry.summary: An adversary establishes a beachhead on an endpoint, moves laterally to obtain administrative access, and pivots to cloud services while maintaining C2 via a multi-hop proxy.

entry.title: Multi-hop Proxy and Tor Infrastructure Activity
entry.summary: An adversary is masking command-and-control traffic by routing it through multi-hop proxies, Tor entry nodes, or tunneling services to bypass perimeter monitoring.

entry.title: Multi-hop proxy and tunnel triage via identity context
entry.summary: An intruder is using a multi-hop proxy or tunneling service to obfuscate C2 traffic, which can be distinguished from legitimate researcher activity by correlating network leads with user risk profiles and local port bindings.

entry.title: Managed Access and Tenant Integrity
entry.summary: An adversary has established persistence via cross-tenant delegated administration or unattended remote support, subsequently deploying autonomous agents that communicate through multi-hop proxies.

entry.title: Network Proxy and Relay Obfuscation Detection
entry.summary: An adversary is using multi-hop proxies or Operational Relay Box (ORB) networks to disguise command-and-control traffic, which can be identified by shell processes making outbound connections to rare external IP addresses and resolving proxy-related DNS infrastructure.

entry.title: Vulnerable Driver Exploitation and Kernel Escalation
entry.summary: An adversary has exploited a public-facing application to stage and load a vulnerable kernel driver, bypassing security controls to gain persistent high-integrity access to the host.

entry.title: Cloud Workload Identity and Network Triage
entry.summary: An adversary uses over-permissioned cloud identities to compromise container workloads, establishing persistence through rare outbound network channels that bypass standard scanning.

entry.title: Cloud Workload Runtime and Exploitation Behavior
entry.summary: An adversary has exploited a public-facing containerized application and is maintaining persistence through binary drift or suspicious shell execution within the workload runtime.

entry.title: Edge AI Artifact Integrity and Data Exfiltration
entry.summary: An adversary has compromised the Edge AI supply chain to poison model artifacts, then manipulated those models via prompt injection to exfiltrate sensitive weights and credentials over high-volume network channels.

entry.title: Appliance Persistence and Identity Abuse
entry.summary: An adversary has modified appliance scheduled tasks to disable MFA and is exfiltrating credentials via native Slack webhook integrations.

entry.title: Collaboration Platform Phishing and Execution
entry.summary: An intruder has compromised an enterprise identity using collaboration tools to bypass email-based controls and execute malicious code via sideloading or malicious dependencies.

entry.title: Build-Time Execution and Secret Harvesting
entry.summary: An attacker has compromised a software dependency to execute malicious code during the build phase, subsequently harvesting cloud and developer credentials from the environment's configuration files.

entry.title: AWS Cloud Identity Takeover Chain
entry.summary: An adversary has gained initial access to a cloud account by brute-forcing the console and performing a password reset, then used that access to establish a presence across multiple projects in the organization.

entry.title: Endpoint Data Staging and Exfiltration
entry.summary: An adversary has staged sensitive information in temporary directories and is exfiltrating that data via rare outbound network connections or DNS lookups.

entry.title: Identity and Cloud Pivot from Web Exploits
entry.summary: An adversary has exploited an internet-facing web server to establish a beachhead and is now manipulating cloud or SaaS identities to persist and reconfigure the environment.

entry.title: Linux Fileless and In-Memory Execution
entry.summary: An adversary is executing malicious code on Linux hosts by staging payloads in memory-backed file descriptors, using interpreter one-liners, or running unlinked binaries to avoid on-disk detection.

entry.title: Kubernetes Service Account Abuse and Escape
entry.summary: An intruder has harvested a service account token from a compromised pod and is using it to deploy a privileged pod for container escape, bypassing standard runtime process detection.

entry.title: AI-Themed Social Engineering and Multi-Stage Fraud
entry.summary: An adversary is using lookalike AI domains and installers to trick users into downloading stealers or performing device-code authentication, leading to token theft and financial fraud.

entry.title: Linux eBPF Rootkit Execution and Manipulation
entry.summary: An intruder has deployed an eBPF rootkit that hides network connections and kernel objects by manipulating syscall returns and tampering with Netlink buffers.

entry.title: AD RMS Discovery and Administrative Reconnaissance
entry.summary: An adversary is identifying on-premises AD RMS clusters via DNS and rights-policy template enumeration before escalating privileges via local group membership to reach the administrative surface.

entry.title: Multi-Stage Intrusion and Ransomware Triage
entry.summary: An adversary has established a beachhead, moved laterally to host-314, exfiltrated data via Node.js to an AI service, and initiated ransomware encryption.

entry.title: Commodity Loader and Multi-Payload PPI Activity
entry.summary: An intruder is using trojanised installers to deploy a multi-stage loader that beacons to rotational C2 domains and installs follow-on backdoors like Insomnia RAT and ARKTunnel.

entry.title: Knight Office Token Theft and Device Persistence
entry.summary: An adversary has stolen Microsoft 365 session tokens via a device-code phishing flow and secured persistence by enrolling an unauthorized rogue device into the Entra ID tenant.

entry.title: Knight Office Phishing Delivery and Redirects
entry.summary: An adversary is using Monday.com redirects and .vu landing pages to deliver Knight Office phishing lures to M365 users.

entry.title: Entra ID Agent User Impersonation and Teams Abuse
entry.summary: An attacker uses the Entra ID Agent User OAuth flow to impersonate an AI agent and dispatch malicious content via Microsoft Teams using Graph API cmdlets.

entry.title: Chrysalis DLL Side-Loading and Execution
entry.summary: An attacker has achieved code execution by placing a malicious DLL in the same directory as a legitimate Bluetooth service, exploiting the search order to side-load code and bypass standard system directory protections.

entry.title: BiTB Phishing to Rogue RMM Persistence
entry.summary: An adversary has used browser-in-the-browser phishing to deceive a user into installing a rogue ScreenConnect instance, which established service-based persistence and executed evasion tools to hide its activity.
